question.problem: Evaluate the integral ${\int }_{C}xy\,\text{d}s$, where the curve $C$ is given in polar form by $r=5\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,$ for $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2}.$
question.worked_solution:
In polar coordinates, the formula for the line integral is given by

$$
{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}s={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta \,.
$$

 

The connection between polar and Cartesian coordinates gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =5\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =5\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta , \\ y & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =5\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =5{sin}^{2}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

So, along our curve, we have $x=5\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ and $y=5{sin}^{2}⁡\theta $, where $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2}.$

Now, if $f(x,y)=xy$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ) & =5\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot 5{sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & =25{sin}^{3}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta } & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}\theta }(5\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ) \\  & =5\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\end{aligned}
$$

and therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  & =\sqrt{(5\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}+(5\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{25({sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta )} \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}xy\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}25{sin}^{3}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot 5\cdot \text{d}\theta  \\  & =125{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{sin}^{3}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this using the substitution $u=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ $\text{d}u=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta $ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}125{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{sin}^{3}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta  & =125{\int }_{0}^{1}{u}^{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =125\cdot \frac{1}{4}{u}^{4}{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{125}{4}({1}^{4}-{0}^{4}) \\  & =\frac{125}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
